diameterInterpretation: Convex light-curve reconstruction. Selected archive volume-equivalent diameter: 93 ±9 km. An alternative pole remains possible. The grid marks unavailable imagery; rotational phase is illustrative.

calibration.uncertaintyKind: Archive estimate of volume-equivalent diameter error; not a bound on local shape accuracy.
calibration.diameterSemantics: Volume-equivalent diameter in the selected DAMIT record; actual source publications and release differences are documented in selectionNotes.
calibration.limitations: The pinned mesh is an inverse model, not a directly sampled surface. No registered reflectance mosaic is supplied by this release; a neutral grid must mark unavailable imagery. Fine-scale craters, regolith and albedo are unresolved. Absolute rotational phase is illustrative. Select pole 1 model 175 (200,52). Hanuš et al. (2013), Tables 2–3, reports this pole and its mirror (18,54), one Keck AO image, and volume-equivalent diameters 93 ±9 and 95 ±9 km; neither is marked rejected. The selected 93-km archive calibration matches the paper. Convex geometry is still inferred from light curves; the AO silhouette calibrates size, not all local topography.
